index_record.dataset_generation_caption:
The figure illustrates the architecture and workflow of AnchorInv, a method for continual learning using anchor-based inversion and fine-tuning across multiple sessions. The global layout is divided into three main sections: Session 0 (Base), Session 1 (Incremental), and Session T (Incremental), arranged vertically and horizontally to show progression over time. A legend at the top right defines visual symbols: input samples (stacked waveforms), embedding network (f_θ), classifier (g_φ), anchor selection function (μ), feature space (cloud with dots), anchor point (hand icon), inversion loss propagation (red arrow), and fine-tuning loss propagation (blue arrow).

In Session 0 (Base), the training dataset D_tr^(0) consists of multiple input samples represented as stacked waveforms. These inputs pass through an embedding network f_θ^(0), which maps them into a feature space depicted as a cloud containing scattered points. An anchor selection function μ processes this feature space to extract anchor points for each class, forming the initial anchor set A^(0), stored as a vertical stack of hand icons.

In Session 1 (Incremental), two data streams are processed. First, the inverted dataset D_inv^(0) — generated by reconstructing features from A^(0) — is fed into f_θ^(0) to produce reconstructed features. This reconstruction is supervised by MAE Loss (Mean Absolute Error), indicated by a red arrow connecting D_inv^(0) to the MAE Loss box. Second, the new training dataset D_tr^(1) is passed through a newly initialized embedding network f_θ^(1). Its outputs are combined with the reconstructed features from D_inv^(0) in the feature space. The classifier g_φ^(1) is trained on class labels via CE Loss (Cross-Entropy Loss), shown by a blue arrow. The anchor selection function μ then extracts anchor points for the new classes, appending them to the anchor set as A^(1), while retaining A^(0).

This pattern continues in Session T (Incremental), where the inverted dataset D_inv^(T−1) — derived from the accumulated anchor sets A^(0) through A^(T−1) — is reconstructed via f_θ^(T−1) and supervised by MAE Loss. Simultaneously, the current training dataset D_tr^(T) is processed by f_θ^(T), whose outputs are combined with reconstructed features from previous sessions (union of D_inv^(t') for t' from 0 to T−2). The classifier g_φ^(T) is fine-tuned using CE Loss on class labels. Finally, anchor points for the new classes are extracted and added to the anchor set as A^(T), extending the memory for future sessions.

Connections are color-coded: red arrows denote inversion loss propagation from inverted samples to MAE Loss, and blue arrows indicate fine-tuning loss propagation from classifiers to CE Loss. The figure emphasizes that anchor sets accumulate across sessions, enabling knowledge retention and guiding inversion for stable continual learning.
